text.p: Finnish confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki Oy said on Friday that profitability had improved between January and August despite only fair sales.

Reporting a 42 percent increase in profit after financial items to 286 million markka ($62.58 million), on sales down two percent at 5.15 billion, Huhtamaki forecast "a clear profit improvement" for the full year over 1995.

"The second third of 1996 brought several structural issues to a close, while profitability continued to improve tangibly despite a moderate overall sales performance," Huhtamaki said in a statement with its results.

Divestment of its pharmaceuticals arm Leiras, combined with the likely sale of its eye medicine business would cause around one billion markka in extraordinary income, which chief executive Timo Peltola said was excluded from its profit outlook.

In confectionery, Huhtamaki said good progress in northern Europe offset weaker North American and southern European sales. Overall, Leaf's top 10 brands expanded by six percent but pruning smaller lines kept sales virtually flat, Huhtamaki said.
In packaging, Huhtamaki said sales volume rose significantly but sales value by only three percent, as lower raw material costs were passed on to finished products.
"New national and regional accounts with major multinational customers are expected to boost volumes further towards year-end and in 1997," Huhtamaki said.
Profitability in ice cream packaging and beverage cups was clearly ahead despite seasonal sales weakness due to poor weather in central and norther Europe, Huhtamaki said.
It said it plans to boost capacity of its Russian and Polish units in the next 12 months in response to dynamic developments in eastern Europe.

Huhtamaki said Leiras -- sold in September -- had shown a strong sales performance. Huhtamaki is still in the process of selling its last non-core business, Star eye medicines, in talks with an unnamed overseas partner. ($1=4.57 Markka)
